messages:
shaun: getting paged by Grafana — gpu-pool-usw2 at 95% alloc, backlog on /v1/generate up 6x in the last 8 min. autoscaler logs show repeated provisioning errors: "quotaExceeded" when creating preemptible instances. spot eviction rate also spiking. customers getting 503 / timeouts. starting an incident, paging oncall. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-15-1945123456 • Severity: Sev2 • Paging: @priya, @alex. Join bridge: https://zoom/bridge/INC-1945123456 • Playbook: /incidents/gpu-provisioning · runbook: gpu-eviction-fallback.md

priya: on it, joining bridge. grabbing autoscaler logs now. tagging SRE. can someone post the top impacted customers?

shaun: quick snapshot — queue depth: 702 -> 4200 in 7m, avg latency 1.2s -> 9.7s, 5xx rate increased from 0.2% -> 7.9%. CPU on control-plane fine, but instance create failures blocking new nodes. suspects: regional quota + cloud api 429s. logs below:

```
Mar 15 19:02:11 autoscaler controller: createNodeGroup(us-west-2, preemptible-gpu): request to cloud api failed: 403 QuotaExceededError: "GPU quota exceeded for region us-west-2"
Mar 15 19:03:05 autoscaler controller: retrying createNodeGroup (attempt 3)
Mar 15 19:03:07 autoscaler controller: createNodeGroup failed: transient 429 TooManyRequests
Mar 15 19:04:30 workload-router: fallback attempt to burst-dedicated returned 0 capacity
Mar 15 19:05:12 eviction-watcher: spot eviction surge: 12 nodes reclaimed in 5m
```

priya: thanks. that matches what i see. autoscaler is in a crashloop-ish backoff because cloud api throttling + quota. two mitigation ideas: 1) enable immediate fallback mapping from spot pools -> small dedicated pool for highest SLAs, 2) temporarily throttle/limit large-batch jobs to protect latency for interactive customers.

alex: +1 on both. how many enterprise customers would we move to dedicated to keep them online? karen can you list impacted accounts with SLAs?

karen (support): pulling from outage dashboard — impacted: "BrightPublish" (prod), "Ledgerly" (prod), "Moneta" (staging but high traffic), ~14 smaller accounts. BrightPublish shows repeated 503s since 19:03. they submitted a ticket. prepping templated message.

jen (sre): i'm spinning up a small dedicated gpu pool manually as a hotfix — provisioning against committed capacity (non-spot) in us-west-2. command: 
```
# ephemeral mitigation - create dedicated node pool
redwoodctl infra nodepool create --region us-west-2 --type p40-dedicated --size 4 --label emergency-fallback
```

priya: doing policy flip for routing: map enterprise tag -> emergency-fallback pool. applying canary to 10% of requests first. config snippet:
```
route: /v1/generate
routing: {
  priority: enterprise
  fallback: emergency-fallback
  canary: 0.10
}
```

alex: i'm calling cloud support now to confirm quota reset ETA and whether additional GPUs can be requested immediately. tagging @cloud-ops-bot to ensure we have a ticket.

cloud-ops-bot: Support ticket opened with provider: TICKET-43321. Severity: high. Request: temporary quota increase and investigation of 429 spike. ETA initial response 15m.

shaun: also seeing a pathological workload from an internal test harness that kicked off large batch runs at 18:58 — throttling them now. commands used: 
```
# throttling heuristic
redwoodctl throttle set --route /v1/generate --qps 50 --reason "emergency; protect latency"
```

priya: initial mitigation status: 1) emergency dedicated pool creation started (jen) 2) routing canary to fallback applied (10%) 3) large-batch throttle applied globally 4) support ticket with cloud provider created. early signs: queue growth slowing after throttle, brightpublish errors decreasing for canary.

karen (support): sent incident notification to BrightPublish CSM + status page update: "Investigating GPU capacity issues in us-west-2; some requests may fail or be delayed. Mitigation in progress."

alex: we need to quantify customer impact for the postmortem — can someone capture % of traffic affected and top 5 clients by error volume? shaun can you grab the metrics?

shaun: pulling counts now — will post in thread. quick numbers: total requests (19:00-19:10): 180k, failed 5xx: 14k (~7.8%). BrightPublish accounted for ~41% of failures, Ledgerly ~12%, others spread.

jen (sre): dedicated pool is now active and nodes registered. routing canary bumped to 30% while we verify stability. no regressions in latency for canary so far.

priya: safety note — don't auto-scale the emergency pool beyond 8 nodes unless we confirm billing/commitment with finance. ping @finance if needed.

alex: agreed. karen, please prepare customer messaging for impacted enterprise customers with ETA update (15-30m). include workaround: set model timeout lower or reduce batch size.

karen (support): message drafted and queued for approval. will add link to status page and zoom bridge.

shaun: tagging followup actions for postmortem: - cloud quota cause analysis - autoscaler resilience to 429/quotaErrors - better preemptible -> dedicated fallback wiring + automated policy - rate-limiting heuristics for noisy tenants - runbook update for manual dedicated pool creation.

incident-bot: Next oncall handoff scheduled at 00:00 UTC — current oncall priya handing to alex. Please record any outstanding actions.

priya: handing off: incident state stable, emergency pool active (4 nodes), canary at 30%, throttle in place, cloud support engaged. outstanding: continue monitoring queue until stable for 45m, confirm cloud quota response, follow up with finance re: temporary commit, prepare postmortem notes. handing to @alex for night. :handshake:

alex: taking over. thanks team — i'll monitor, coordinate with cloud support, and own comms for next 3 hours. priya — if anything changes ping me immediately.

karen (support): support updates queued every 15m to status page. next scheduled update 19:40.

jen (sre): will capture autoscaler debug logs and upload to incident repo: /incidents/1945123456/artifacts/autoscaler-debug.log

shaun: closing bridge in 10m if steady. otherwise keep it open. good work. :thumbsup:
